title: Eval Harness & Model Onboarding Playbook — Applied ML and Evals
author: Emily Chen
body:
Overview

This document defines Redwood's standardized eval harness, the model onboarding checklist, recommended prompt sets and benchmarks, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and a regression triage playbook. It is the canonical internal reference for Applied ML engineers and product owners responsible for model evaluation and deployment readiness.

Scope

- Eval harness architecture and ownership
- Prompt set creation and benchmark conventions
- Model onboarding gates and checklist
- Quality guardrails (metrics, thresholds, monitoring)
- Quantization profile recommendations and validation
- Regression triage and rollback procedure

Definitions

- Eval Harness (evald): the standardized Redwood evaluation pipeline (service name: redwood-eval-harness) used to run deterministic and stochastic tests across model candidates.
- Prompt Set: curated input/output pairs used to measure functional and quality metrics. Stored in s3://redwood-evals/prompt-sets/ by canonical name.
- Regression: a measurable degradation in a tracked metric after a model change (>= 3% drop or absolute change crossing threshold).

1) Eval Harness (redwood-eval-harness)

Purpose:
- Provide reproducible, versioned runs for accuracy, toxicity, hallucination, latency, and cost-estimation.
- Support parallel runs across model variants (fp16, int8, quantized variants).

Architecture:
- Runner: Kubernetes job that pulls model artifact (registry reference) and runs tests; triggered by CI or manually via the eval CLI.
- Storage: results written to S3 (s3://redwood-evals/results/{model}/{run-id}) and indexed to the eval database for dashboards.
- Metrics: metrics emitted to Datadog with tags: model:name, model:version, eval:run_id, prompt_set, quant_profile.

How to run (examples):

CLI (local quick-run):
```
# Run canonical eval with prompt set 'summary-200' and quant profile 'int8-fast'
evald run --model ref:my-model:v1 --prompt-set summary-200 --quant-profile int8-fast --output s3://redwood-evals/results/my-model/v1-20260110
```

CI integration (example job snippet):
```
jobs:
  run-evals:
    steps:
      - name: checkout
      - name: run evals
        run: evald run --model $MODEL_REF --prompt-set smoke-suite --report-path $REPORT_PATH
```

Output and expectations:
- Each run produces: run.json, metrics.json, example-failures.json, and a CSV summary.
- All runs must include seed and randomization metadata for stochastic tests.

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarks

Organization:
- Prompt sets live in s3://redwood-evals/prompt-sets/{category}/{prompt-set-name}. Each set has metadata JSON describing source, author, coverage, and known limitations.
- Categories: summarization, instruction-following, safety, math, code, retrieval, dialogue.

Creation guidelines:
1. Balance: include both short and long inputs, diverse token distributions, and realistic user phrasing.
2. Ground truth: when possible include human-annotated references and multiple acceptable outputs.
3. Edge cases: include intentionally adversarial and out-of-distribution examples for robustness.
4. Versioning: bump the prompt-set semantic version when examples are added/removed (>5% change).

Benchmark naming and baselines:
- Naming: {category}-{size}-{year}, e.g., summarization-200-2025.
- Baselines: every benchmark must include at least one Redwood-verified baseline model and historical best-known score.
- Key metrics: ROUGE/ROUGE-L, BLEU (if applicable), Exact Match, F1, perplexity, and task-specific metrics (e.g., pass@k for code).

3) Model Onboarding Checklist

Mandatory gating criteria (must pass to be eligible for production rollout):
- Eval harness: complete canonical eval run (smoke-suite + category-specific sets) with documented results in S3.
- Quality metrics: all required metrics must meet thresholds in the Quality Guardrails section.
- Latency & cost: P50 and P95 latency compared to baseline and token cost estimate within agreed budget.
- Security & privacy: ensure model artifacts and data handling conform to data-management policy (link in references).
- Documentation: model card + evaluation report uploaded to the model catalog.

Onboarding steps (numbered):
1. Register model in model-catalog with metadata (owner, training data, license, intended use).
2. Run smoke-suite and record run_id.
3. Run full eval suite for target workloads and quant profiles.
4. Submit evaluation PR with results and proposed rollout plan (canary percentages, rollback criteria).
5. Review by applied-ml reviewers (listed on PR).
6. Schedule canary deployment and post-canary evaluation.

Checklist table (text):
- Model card: Yes/No
- Smoke eval: run_id
- Full eval: run_id(s)
- Quant profiles tested: list
- Security review: Y/N

4) Quality Guardrails

Primary metrics and thresholds (example baseline numbers; teams must set product-specific thresholds):
- Accuracy/Task metric: No regression > 1.5% relative vs baseline (or configurable threshold).
- Safety (toxicity): P95 toxicity score <= 0.02 absolute or no increase >10% relative.
- Hallucination rate: decrease in knowledge-grounded task F1 of >2% triggers triage.
- Latency: P95 inference latency increase must be <= 20% vs baseline for dedicated deployments.
- Cost/unit: per-token cost increase tolerated <= 15% for a major model upgrade.

Monitoring and Alerts:
- Datadog monitors: eval.regression.detect (alerts when metric deltas exceed thresholds).
- Slack channel: #applied-ml-evals for automated run completions, failures, and regression alerts.
- Weekly quality dashboard: auto-generated summary of top regressions, new models onboarded, and outstanding triage items.

Quality gates for rollout:
- Green: all metrics within thresholds -> proceed to canary 5%.
- Amber: 1 metric slightly out of threshold -> manual review required; canary limited to 1-2% and run targeted evals.
- Red: >1 critical metric regressed -> block rollout and initiate regression triage.

5) Quantization Profiles

Profiles maintained under confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles; stored artifacts: quant-profile-{name}.yaml

Recommended profiles (examples):
- fp16-balanced: default for high-accuracy low-latency workloads.
- int8-fast: aggressive size reduction prioritizing throughput; validate generative quality.
- int8-safe: int8 with calibrated per-channel scaling and KV-cache preservation; preferred for safety-sensitive deployments.

Validation steps for a quant profile:
1. Run canonical evals with same random seed across fp16 and quantized model.
2. Compare task metrics and sample-level diffs (example-failures.json).
3. Run synthetic stress tests: long context (up to target max-seq), KV cache retention, and multi-turn dialogues.
4. Approve if no regression beyond thresholds in Quality Guardrails.

Common failure modes to watch for:
- Tokenization misalignment between training and runtime leading to shifted outputs.
- Increased hallucination frequency on knowledge tasks.
- Degraded multi-turn coherency due to KV cache precision loss.

6) Regression Triage Playbook

Triggering conditions:
- Automated alert from eval.regression.detect OR post-deployment customer report with reproducible test case.

Immediate triage steps (first 60 minutes):
1. Acknowledge ticket in PagerDuty and create a triage thread in #applied-ml-evals with run_id and short description.
2. Capture failing examples and reproduce locally using evald reproduce --run-id {run-id}.
3. Determine scope: is regression limited to a prompt set, quant profile, region, or rollout cohort?
4. If regression is severe (customer-facing outage or major metric drop), initiate rollback per deployment playbook.

Diagnosis checklist (next 4 hours):
- Check model artifact differences (weights, tokenizer, codegen changes).
- Compare eval metrics and failure examples between baseline and new run.
- Re-run with higher sampling seeds and beam search to confirm.
- Validate quantization profile differences and re-test fp16 baseline.
- Check infra differences: runtime library versions, kernel updates, or serving changes.

Mitigation and rollback:
- Canary-scale rollback: revert canary cohort to previous model and monitor for recovery.
- Global rollback: if regression persists in canary and affects >5% traffic, follow oncall-and-incident-response/deployment rollback runbook.
- Hotfix options: temporary routing to fallback model variant (lower capacity but verified), or apply configuration fixes (temperature, sampling, prompt prefixing).

Postmortem and prevention:
1. Produce postmortem within 72 hours with owner, timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and prevention.
2. Update prompt sets and test coverage if failures were due to uncovered scenarios.
3. Add targeted evaluations to the smoke-suite to prevent future regressions.

7) Ownership, SLAs and Review Cadence

- Owners: Applied ML team owns eval harness and onboarding process. Model owners are responsible for passing checks and providing triage support.
- SLAs: evaluation runs requested by product teams should be scheduled within 48 hours for smoke-suite and within 5 business days for full-suite runs (depending on fleet availability).
- Reviews: quarterly model catalog reviews; monthly quality dashboard review meetings.

8) Appendix: Example evaluation metadata (textified)

Example run.json excerpt:
```
{
  "run_id": "eval-20260110-abc123",
  "model_ref": "registry:redwood/my-model:v2",
  "prompt_set": "summarization-200-2025",
  "quant_profile": "int8-fast",
  "seed": 42,
  "metrics": {"rouge_l": 0.412, "toxicity_p95": 0.008}
}
```
